title: Componentwise gluing of set-sheaf maps in a containing universe
statement: Let C be a category with pullbacks, J a Grothendieck topology, and {f_a : X_a → U} a family generating a J-covering sieve [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. All indexing types and section sets lie in a universe containing both site universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let F and G be sheaves of sets on C/U. For each a let s_a : F|_{X_a} → G|_{X_a} be a natural transformation, where restriction is sectionwise composition along Over.map [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. On X_a ×_U X_b identify the two composites to U by the canonical natural isomorphism with identity underlying arrow. Suppose G transports s_b(x) to s_a applied to the transported x for every overlap object and section, including a=b. Then there exists a unique natural transformation t : F → G whose component on every object over X_a is the specified component of s_a.

proof.text: For V→U pull back the covering family to V_a=V×_U X_a→V. Covering stability and the slice topology make this a cover in C/U. For x∈F(V), restrict x to V_a and apply s_a. On V_a×_V V_b the two results agree: naturality restricts each s_a to the corresponding object of C/(X_a×_U X_b), and the assumed overlap equation identifies the results, including the identity-arrow comparison of composites to U.

The sheaf axiom for G gives a unique amalgamation t_V(x). For W→V the restrictions of G(W→V)(t_V(x)) and t_W(F(W→V)(x)) agree after the pullback cover of W by naturality of every s_a, hence agree by separatedness. This proves naturality of t.

If V→U factors through X_a, its graph into V×_U X_a is a section of the covering projection. Restrict the amalgamation equation for index a along this graph and apply naturality of s_a. The two composite arrows are identities, so t_V equals s_a on that object. Finally any two natural maps with these local formulas agree on all V_a; separatedness of G makes them equal on every V. This also proves the empty-cover case, when all G(V) are singletons.

theorem overSheafMapGluing
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {I : Type (max u v w)}
    (U : C) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ a, X a ⟶ U)
    (hcov : Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U)
    (F G : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u v w)))
    (s : ∀ a, (Over.map (f a)).op ⋙ F.obj ⟶ (Over.map (f a)).op ⋙ G.obj)
    (hs : ∀ (a b : I) (V : Over (pullback (f a) (f b)))
      (x : F.obj.obj (op ((Over.map (pullback.snd (f a) (f b)) ⋙
        Over.map (f b)).obj V))),
      G.obj.map
        (((Over.mapComp _ _).symm ≪≫
          Over.mapCongr _ _ (pullback.condition (f := f a) (g := f b)) ≪≫
          Over.mapComp _ _).hom.app V).op ((s b).app _ x) =
        (s a).app _ (F.obj.map
          (((Over.mapComp _ _).symm ≪≫
            Over.mapCongr _ _ (pullback.condition (f := f a) (g := f b)) ≪≫
            Over.mapComp _ _).hom.app V).op x)) :
    ∃! t : F.obj ⟶ G.obj,
      ∀ (a : I) (V : (Over (X a))ᵒᵖ)
        (x : F.obj.obj ((Over.map (f a)).op.obj V)),
        t.app _ x = (s a).app V x
